newsitem.title: USA: CalPERS to invest $150 million in Behrman fund.
newsitem.headline: CalPERS to invest $150 million in Behrman fund.

text.p: The California Public Employees' Retirement System (CalPERS) said on Tuesday it would invest $150 million in a Behrman Capital buyout fund focusing on emerging growth companies.

The Behrman Capital II fund will target buyouts of companies in information technology, health care and contract manufacturing industries, including many California-based companies, CalPERS said in a statement.

"We intend to continue to develop strong ties with Behrman Capital and other top firms in the private equity field that will help us capture superior returns for the fund," Charles Valdes, chair of CalPERS investment committee, said.

Under its so-called "Alternative Investment Management" strategy, CalPERS is expected to commit $500 million to $1 billion a year to new direct investments and $1 billion to $1.5 billion a year to partnerships.
CalPERS previously invested $25 million in Behrman Capital I in 1994 and an additional $25 million in 1995. It has been one of CalPERS' top performing funds, the pension system said.
Behrman Capital, which was founded in 1992, is headquartered in New York and San Francisco.
CalPERS is the largest public pension fund in the United States and the third largest in the world, with assets totaling more than $113 billion.
The fund provides retirement and health benefits to more than one million public employees and their families.
